## Preserved failure: native correctability does not justify injection

Consider instead a deterministic physical X1 before V. The uninjected channel is an exactly correctable isometry and occupies majority gauge g=1. Uniformly adding the same injection produces

    H_Z=diag(1,1,-1,-1)/4.

Thus it violates the qualitative CP-nonnegative-contrast promise even though its unsigned marginal is full and its signed matrix is invertible. The raw Z sign is `U[Z tensor diag(1,1,-1,-1)]U†`, not `U[Z tensor I4]U†`. Together with the raw X sign it defines a consistent but gauge-dependent wrong logical frame. It decodes the old X1 payload perfectly; if a later allowed physical error is X2, that decoder performs logical X and has Bell loss one, whereas the true majority frame still has loss zero. The receiver guard checks both cases on all coherent matrix units.

This is NOT a counterexample to the received iid-bitflip witness: deterministic X1 is outside that identical-flip probability family and outside the calibration positivity promise. It is an exact obstruction to deriving the exploration operation's correctness merely from native correctability, full unsigned occupation, or an observed nonzero signed gap. No finite transcript certifies the trusted model or its unseen completions.
